summary:
NEBULA is an educational space mission design game that runs in the browser, offline, from a single HTML file. Players choose a mission (Earth orbit, lunar orbit or Mars orbit), design a spacecraft under real limits of mass, power, propellant and budget, and then fly the mission day by day. Orbits, Hohmann transfers, delta-v, eclipses, solar flux and communication delay are computed with real physics equations. Neuron Core, the game’s AI assistant, combines engineering rules, a small neural network trained in the browser, and an optimizer to diagnose the design and suggest improvements, always leaving the final decision to the player. During the mission, solar storms and communication blackouts force real choices, and a Twin Mode compares two designs under identical events. A final analytics screen explains exactly why the mission succeeded or failed. A companion Google Colab notebook verifies every equation numerically. 
NEBULA turns the challenge of mission design into something students can play, test and understand.
details:
What it does. NEBULA is an educational game where you design, launch and fly a space mission. You pick a mission (Earth orbit, lunar orbit or Mars orbit), build a spacecraft under real limits of mass, power, propellant and budget, and then fly it day by day, making decisions when solar storms, communication blackouts or power failures strike. A final screen explains exactly why the mission succeeded or failed.

How it works. The game computes orbital velocity, Hohmann transfers, rocket delta-v, eclipses, solar flux and signal delay with real physics equations. Neuron Core, the in-game assistant, combines engineering rules, a small neural network trained in the browser and an optimizer to diagnose a design and suggest improvements, but the player always decides. Events are generated from a seed, so Twin Mode can compare two designs under identical conditions.

Benefits and impact. Students learn engineering trade-offs by doing, not by reading. Every result shows its variables, units and assumptions. It runs offline from a single HTML file, in English and Spanish, with no installation.

Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript (Canvas), Python for building and testing, Playwright for automated tests, and a Google Colab notebook (NumPy, Matplotlib) that verifies every equation numerically with 38 checks.

Creativity and design choices. We made the physics the source of truth and the visuals a way to show it. We also kept the AI explainable and separated rules from machine learning, so the game never overpromises what the neural network can do.
